title: All-hands spotlight: rapid-fire customer + team stories (scratch)
content:
Purpose: two 90–120s spotlight segments + single closing mic (3 min total). Personal scratchpad for framing, not final script.

Constraints: keep it tight (no slides), human stories > metrics, leave one line for CEO handoff. Try to surface one unexpected win and one empathetic failure.

Opening (10–15s):
- Quick hook: 'I want to celebrate a tiny change that saved a customer from a messy Friday.'
- Why short stories: relatable, high signal for org values (reliability, craft, curiosity).

Spotlight A (90s) — "Prefix cache saved a major demo"
- Who: SRE on-call (Jordan P.) + Solutions Engineer (Sahana)
- Setup (10s): large fintech customer demo failing due to cold-start slowness, high token counts in multi-turn flow.
- Action (30s): SRE enabled a short-lived prefix/KV cache and tuned request routing to Dedicated fallback — rolled in ~25m during the demo prep window.
- Outcome (20s): demo proceeded, customer signed pilot LOI; engineers later made the cache config default for similar accounts.
- Why it matters (15s): shows ops + SE collaboration, productizable runtime tweak, $ saved in seat time and credibility.
- Note-to-self: ask Jordan for exact latency numbers (p95 pre/post) and a 1-line quote to include in final draft.

Spotlight B (90s) — "Regression caught by a prompt-based eval"
- Who: Applied ML (Katya) + Product QA (Ravi)
- Setup (15s): after a model swap in staging, a subtle hallucination pattern emerged in long-context Q&A.
- Action (30s): Quick eval harness run against critical prompt set; engineer rolled a guardrail that routed queries above 512 tokens to a safer model variant.
- Outcome (20s): prevented regression reaching production during a customer uplift test; small UX change rolled better than expected.
- Why it matters (15s): demonstrates the end-to-end eval + routing story we keep pitching — technical safety + product benefit.
- Note-to-self: confirm which prompt set triggered the alert (eval id) and grab a short quote from Katya about detection time.

Mic handoff and call-to-action (30–45s):
- Transition line: 'Two quick wins — one operational, one evaluative — both thanks to people making fast, measurable choices.'
- Ask for applause for on-call/SE/AM collaboration.
- CTA to org: 'If you have a 90s story of a tiny change that mattered, drop it in #all-hands-stories. We'll feature a few every month.'
- Close with CEO handoff: 'Over to Samir for the roadmap snapshot.'

Backup Q&A prompts (for on-the-fly):
- Q: "Did the cache introduce correctness risk?" A: short: no; scoped TTL, monitoring, quick rollback. (Follow up w/ Jordan for specifics.)
- Q: "Why route long context to a different model vs. fix model?" A: short: immediate mitigation while we evaluate model finetuning/quantization cost tradeoffs.

Personal notes / reminders (to finish before final):
- Get exact p95 numbers from Jordan and the LOI month value estimate from Sahana.
- Grab eval id and sample prompt/response from Katya + permission to paraphrase.
- Draft 2 versions: 90s spoken and 45s ultra-short (for time compression).
- Check with CEO on preferred handoff phrasing.

Unresolved / TBD (why this is a scratchpad):
- Need one-line legal-safe phrasing for customer mention if LOI is not public. Consider anonymizing customer name.
- Decide whether to include a small slide in backup deck with before/after latency chart (ask Release Eng for a png export).

Tone notes: conversational, lightly technical but avoid jargon for non-ENG audience, spotlight the humans not the tech. Keep the two stories contrastive: ops vs eval.

End-of-pad 'notes to self' micro checklist:
- [ ] Jordan latency numbers
- [ ] Sahana LOI sign date/value
- [ ] Katya eval id + quote
- [ ] Legal greenlight for anonymized customer shoutout
- [ ] Final 90s script to Mirabelle by 2026-03-18

Raw lines that might be used verbatim (pick 1–2):
- 'Small fixes compound: a 25-minute ops tweak turned into a pilot conversation.'
- 'We caught something because someone wrote a test that asked the hard question out loud.'

Footer (scratch):
- Archive note: move final text to confluence page once approved (linked_artifacts[0]).
- If trimmed to 45s, drop the outcomes detail and keep the human hook + CTA.

----
Scratch metadata: last jot at 2026-03-12 09:33 PT. This is a private personal draft — will iterate with Jordan / Katya / Sahana then push to #all-hands-drafts for review.
